resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO), Resale/Rental Inspection
resale_co.lead_time: Schedule the inspection at least 5 calendar days before settlement; requests 4 calendar days or less before settlement pay the higher fee.
requirements: House numbers: numerals at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, fixed to the house and visible from the street (mailbox or lamp post numbers not accepted)
Smoke alarm on every level, including the bottom of the basement stairs at the ceiling
Smoke alarm within 10 feet of all bedroom doors and one on the ceiling of every bedroom
Hardwired smoke alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Smoke alarms under 10 years old and working; battery alarms must be 10-year sealed type
CO alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms, under 10 years old and working
Fire extinguisher (2019 checklist): 2A-10B:C, under 10 pounds, mounted on its bracket within 10 feet of the kitchen in the path of exit
Homes with a monitored low-voltage fire alarm system need a test certificate from an alarm contractor at the inspection
Owner certifies all structures meet zoning and no rubbish, debris or bulk trash is left before the new occupant moves in

fees.label: CCO inspection, more than 4 calendar days before settlement (per dwelling unit, includes one reinspection)
fees.quote: Prior to inspection, Owners are required to submit an online application along with the fee of $75.

fees.label: CCO inspection requested 4 calendar days or less before settlement
fees.quote: Requests for inspection received four (4) calendar days or less prior to settlement or renter's move in date will require an inspection fee of $125.

fees.label: Each additional reinspection after the one included (Ordinance 2019-9)
fees.quote: These inspection fees shall include one reinspection. If any additional reinspections are needed, there shall be a $25 reinspection fee.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Submit the online CCO Application on GovPilot (choose Resale) and pay the fee. Schedule the inspection at least 5 calendar days before settlement; requests 4 calendar days or less before settlement cost $125. Questions: Resale/Rental Inspectors at 609-267-5723 ext. 200.
resale_co.contact_title: Resale/Rental Inspector (also Danny Ernst, Resale/Rental Inspector, same number)

evidence.quote: Per Ordinance 2010-4; 385-4 a Certificate of Continued Occupancy inspection is required for all property resales or rental units whenever there is a change of occupancy and/or ownership.
Prior to inspection, Owners are required to submit an online application along with the fee of $75.
Ord. 2019-9 Change of Occupancy and Inspection Fees
Vincent Knott Position Resale/Rental Inspector Phone Number (609) 267-5723 ext. 200
Inspections must be scheduled at least five (5) calendar days prior to the settlement date or renter's move in date

I certify that this dwelling and all other structures on the property meet the zoning requirements of Eastampton Township I attest to the fact that no rubbish/debris/bulk garbage will be left on this property prior to new occupancy.
Numbers are numerical characters, contrasting color from the house, at least 4” high, permanently affixed to the house & visible from the street.

resale_co.notes: The live Resale/Rental Inspections page (eastampton.com/rental, behind a Cloudflare bot check, read through a text reader) now calls it a Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO), still lists the $75 fee and the $125 fee for requests 4 calendar days or less before settlement, and names two Resale/Rental Inspectors, Vincent Knott and Danny Ernst (609-267-5723 ext. 200); David Shaw is no longer listed. The page links Ordinance 2019-9 (Change of Occupancy and Inspection Fees), which could not be opened live; its $25 extra-reinspection fee and 5-day scheduling rule come from an Internet Archive copy of the same ordinance (scanned PDF read visually earlier). Inspector emails are behind contact forms, so no email is recorded. The inspection checklist on the live site (media/2451) could not be opened; the archived November 2019 checklist still lists a fire extinguisher. Rentals built before 1978 also need a lead-based paint inspection with a separate fee (Ordinance 2024-10); that is rental only.

requirements: The Township's CCO inspection checklist (November 2019) covers smoke alarms, CO alarms and a mounted 2A-10B:C fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen, so these are checked at the resale inspection
Smoke and CO alarms must be under 10 years old; battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed type

authorities.name: Eastampton Township Local Enforcing Agency (Fire Prevention Bureau, Office of the Fire Marshal)
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate resale smoke/CO certificate application or fee was found. The smoke, CO and extinguisher items are on the Township's resale CCO checklist; ask the Resale/Rental Inspector or the Fire Marshal whether the CCO inspection also issues the smoke/CO certificate.

evidence.quote: The Eastampton LEA is administered by Eastampton Township, and is outside of the Fire Department command structure.
in Eastampton Township, both roles are filled by Yunus Boduroglu, and the titles are used interchangeably.
LEAID: 0311-001 Enf Auth. District Fire Official Yunus Bodugroglu Phone (609) 267-5723
A copy of the alarm certification provided by the alarm contractor must be presented to the WTES inspector at the time of the inspection.

fire_cert.notes: The DCA Q3 2026 registry codes Eastampton as a fire district (D) enforcing agency, but the Township's live Fire Marshal page says the LEA is administered by the Township, outside the fire department, with Yunus Boduroglu as Fire Marshal and Fire Official (office 609-267-5723 ext. 203, firemarshal@eastampton.com; the state directory spells it 'Bodugroglu'). The state directory (survey 5/18/2026) names 'Westampton Twp Emergency Ser' as the smoke detector compliance contact, and the archived 2019 CCO checklist refers to a 'WTES' inspector, which suggests Westampton Township Emergency Services does the resale smoke/CO inspection under a shared arrangement, but no official page says so directly. No separate resale smoke certificate fee was found; the Fire Marshal's online payment page lists only non-life hazard registration fees, and the Fees and Pre-Inspection Checklist covers business inspections.

open_questions: Whether the Township CCO inspection also issues the state smoke/CO certificate, or whether Westampton Township Emergency Services issues it separately, and at what fee.
The $25 extra-reinspection fee is from Ordinance 2019-9 (archived copy); confirm it is still current.
Whether the current CCO checklist still requires a fire extinguisher after P.L.2025, c.19 (the live checklist could not be opened).
